claims: Artemis II mission features the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion capsule.
Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026, for a 10-day lunar flyby.
Artemis II launch time is April 1, 2026, 6:35 p.m. EDT.
Artemis II duration is approximately 10 days.
Artemis II mission goal is to test Orion spacecraft systems, crew capability, and safety for future moon landings.
Artemis II trajectory is a free-return loop around the Moon, passing 4,700 miles above the surface.
Artemis II crew includes Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II tests systems for future lunar landings including Artemis IV in 2028.
Artemis program aims to establish a sustainable human presence on the Moon by the late 2020s.
Artemis IV in 2028 is planned as the first crewed landing of the Artemis program.
Artemis program uses lunar experiences to prepare for the first human missions to Mars.
Artemis I in 2022 was an uncrewed test of SLS and Orion.
Artemis II in April 2026 is a crewed lunar flyby.
Artemis III in mid-2027 is now a low-Earth orbit mission to test systems.
Artemis IV in 2028 is planned as a human lunar landing.
